text:
aisha (Partnerships): Heads-up  Skylimit (vendor) wants a three-way launch: AWS Marketplace listing, downloadable model artifact for on-prem integrators, and a co-branded edge appliance bundle with HW partner. Need alignment on licensing, geo-restrictions, and announcement responsibilities.

 tom (Legal): Quick Q: do we allow vendors to grant redistributable rights that permit inclusion in partner appliances? We need clarity on sublicensing vs redistribution.

 aisha (Partnerships): They propose a dual-route: (1) Marketplace AMI + managed listing, (2) downloadable tarball under our portal, and (3) partner appliance image. They want one contract covering all.

 rachel (Marketplace): For AWS/GCP marketplaces we need specific packaging: AMI / container image + manifest. Downloadable tarballs are fine but must pass our packaging spec. Also pricing SKU must be separate: "hosted API", "managed AMI", "downloadable license".

 noah (Eng): Technical risk note: appliance bundle requires a certified runtime + quantization profile. We should require vendor to provide a validated runtime binary or a `compatibility manifest` with checksums and CPU/GPU variant tests. Otherwise support burden falls to us.

 tom (Legal): I recommend the contract include: vendor attests IP rights to model and training data; vendor grants Redwood a limited sublicense to distribute as specified (AMI, download, appliance image) but prohibits onward resale to other marketplaces. Also require vendor to indemnify for IP claims.

 aisha (Partnerships): Can we be stricter about downstream modifications? The hardware partner will likely want to repack images for appliance provisioning. We should allow repackaging for deployment but disallow re-selling the base model weight as a standalone product.

 on-board-bot: action-item: partnership-onboard checklist created for Skylimit. Pending items: legal redline, packaging spec, HW compatibility test plan, export review. Due in 72h.

 tom (Legal): Suggested clause snippet: ```
Sublicense & Distribution: Vendor grants Redwood a non-exclusive sublicense to distribute the Model in three formats: (i) cloud marketplace images, (ii) downloadable artifacts via Redwood portal, and (iii) hardware appliance images for contracted partners. Such sublicense does NOT permit Redwood or its partners to resell the Model as a standalone weight bundle to third-party marketplaces without Vendor's prior written consent. Vendor represents and warrants it has authority to grant sublicenses for compiled/quantized artifacts and will provide provenance metadata and checksums for each artifact.
```

 rachel (Marketplace): Also include a marketplace-ready `manifest.json` requirement (example below) so the listing automation can validate artifacts: ```
{
  "name": "skylimit-13b-q4",
  "formats": ["safetensors-q4", "pth-int8"],
  "runtime_compat": ["redwood-runtime-v2"],
  "checksums": {"safetensors-q4": "sha256:..."}
}
```

 noah (Eng): I'll draft a minimal compatibility test harness that runs the model through `redwood-runtime-v2` smoke tests and verifies token-level output hash for a stable prompt. We should require vendor to pass this before any marketplace listing.

 aisha (Partnerships): Marketing: Skylimit wants a big joint launch + HW partner press release. I propose a staged cadence: private SI canary (3 SIs) -> marketplace GA (NA/EU) -> appliance public announcement. Downloads geoblocked until export sign-off for APAC.

 tom (Legal): Export controls: require vendor confirmation of export classification and that the artifacts don't violate regional controls. Add explicit embargo clauses: Redwood can delay distribution in certain jurisdictions pending compliance.

 rachel (Marketplace): For AWS/GCP we need lead time to create product listings and billing SKUs. Recommend 10 business days post-legal sign-off. Also: billing model for appliance bundles needs a separate transfer-licensing fee line item.

 noah (Eng): Support implications: downloadable artifacts mean customers may self-host; we should gate support tiering. Maybe only enterprise customers get 24/7 SLA for downloadable artifacts; otherwise community support. Put that in partner agreement.

 aisha (Partnerships): Good. Action items: (1) @tom produce redline with export & IP attestations + sublicense limits (due 48h); (2) @noah publish compatibility test harness and test criteria (due 48h); (3) @rachel draft marketplace manifest template and SKU mapping (due 72h); (4) partnerships PM to draft co-marketing timeline and SI canary list (due 72h).

 tom (Legal): I'll add a short vendor checkbox: "I confirm authority to sublicense compiled models and consent to provide provenance and checksums." Also add indemnity and a 90-day take-down clause for IP disputes.

 on-board-bot: Checklist update: legal: pending; eng test harness: pending; marketplace manifest: pending; export review: queued. Deadline reminders set. :alarm_clock: 

 aisha (Partnerships): Thanks team. One last note: avoid language in public docs like "fully open distribution". Use "partner-deliverable" or "downloadable under license". We'll review the announcement copy before publish. :memo:
